We definitely need much more polish on the VFX side. But this polish is more about connecting the screens to each other rather than gameplay itself
• For example, we need animations for rewards and events in the main menu. At the same time, the level win animation in their game feels very satisfying, whereas ours feels a bit weak at the moment

• Regarding events, I think There are definitely 2–3 more events that we absolutely need. Of course, the more, the better
• For events, they have almost the exact same event list we had planned for DD, and their event variety is greater than ours. This means that after level 20+, players always have a new goal to work toward. In other words, players constantly have a locked event sitting in one corner of the screen. Most of the events are auto-participate types, so players inevitably find themselves in a flow
• Additionally, for players who follow events, they have a time-based “x2 multiplier” currency. This allows players to earn x2 tokens from levels for a certain period of time, enabling them to progress further in the events. As a result, this is a factor that increases session time for players who are interested in events
• When I checked the currently active events today, most of them were single-player events. There were 5 single-player events and 2 competition-type events.

I think their monetization strategy works as follows
• You don’t earn coins from levels. You can only earn coins from events
• The 2 competition events are built around resetting your progress when you fail a level (one is similar to our Axe Arena, and the other is like the [PERSON_NAME_64564] event from DD). • In gameplay, I failed levels not because of a timer but mostly due to wrong matches. In that case, it’s technically my fault—but if I want to make up for my mistake and avoid losing my progress, I need to spend coins

Lastly, I can add this: you can really feel your progress in the game.
• If you repair structures in the meta, you progress through the main screen
• If you follow events, you likely feel like you’re progressing up until level 50 by unlocking new events
• And on the gameplay side, you feel your progress by playing levels with different objects or by unlocking new objects in certain levels

I dug into the CSV and measured *level-to-level continuation* as users[L+1] ÷ users[L] within each A/B group, then related that to *win rate* and *average level duration* per level.
*What the data says*
1. *Win rate matters more than duration, especially in the MF group.*
    ◦ In MF, win rate is a strong predictor of continuing to the next level even after controlling for level index and duration. A +10 pp increase in win rate predicts about *+2.7 pp higher continuation*. Duration is not statistically meaningful.
    ◦ In Default, neither win rate nor duration is strongly predictive after controlling for level, though There is a mild positive trend for duration.
2. *Same-level comparison (MF vs Default) points to win rate, not duration.*
    ◦ Regressing *Δ continuation (MF − Default)* on *Δ win rate* and *Δ duration* across levels shows a positive effect for *Δ win rate* and near-zero for *Δ duration*. In short, when MF has higher win rate than Default at the same level, MF also tends to have higher continuation; duration differences do not explain the gap.
3. *Quintile contrast for intuition.*
    ◦ MF: levels in the top win-rate quintile have *~7.1 pp* higher continuation than the bottom quintile. The analogous contrast for duration is *~1.0 pp*.
    ◦ Default: win-rate contrast *~4.1 pp*, duration *~1.6 pp*.
I put summary tables, the diff-in-diff regression, and two quick scatterplots in the workspace above so you can skim the patterns visually.
*Actionable takeaways*
• *Prioritize raising win rate on low-continuation levels*, particularly in MF. Early candidates where both continuation and win rate are under 90% include:
    ◦ *MF:* Levels *4* (win 0.76, cont 0.82), *8* (0.63, 0.84), *12* (0.69, 0.85), *9* (0.85, 0.88), *7* (0.79, 0.89).
• *Default:* Levels *9* (0.77, 0.85), *23* (0.81, 0.89).
    ◦  These are listed in the “Early-Level Opportunities” table above.
• *Tune difficulty, not session length, to lift level-to-level retention.*
•  Use the knobs you already control (symbol count, spawn rates, pity, extra tiles, etc.) to nudge win rate up where continuation dips. The MF variant appears *more sensitive to win rate*, so small difficulty fixes should have noticeable retention impact There.
• *Keep durations in a comfortable band rather than pushing them up.*
•  Across levels, *longer duration does not systematically improve continuation*. Aim for a smooth time-to-win profile, but do not expect longer stages to move retention.
*Notes and next steps*
• A few continuation values exceed 1.0. That happens when distinct user counts rise between adjacent levels (data grouping, late entries, or session stitching). It does not change the directional conclusions but is worth cleaning in the next pass.
• For causality, the ideal follow-up is *user-level* modeling: logistic regression or survival analysis with last outcome (win/loss), time on level, retries, boosts, and player fixed effects. That will tighten the estimate of how much a win on level L drives starting L+1.

<@EMPLOYEE_0012_SLACK_ID> Fusing cards vs. wildcards
We got new items and I made levels for your variant (Pool ball and cue stick!)

Card Fusion is better for long-term engagement Imo because it's controlled better by the player but requires more complexity and UI work. If we're using the word same semantically. And the idea of fusion is mostly tied to binary card equipment (owned cs not owned).

Overall, the wildcard is better for amount-based card upgrades. Burning cards for binary card systems. And [USERNAME_14652] did both. For both spectrum in a better way, for upgrade it uses scroll just like bones and for rarity ascension, uses the fusion (similar to wildcards actually).  So for our hybrid, we have a card system more like crash royale and what he did can suit better with us.

I like the crash royale system but our deck has less slots and equipped cards' effects are indirect. But on the other hand, every owned card matters in our game. So I think we should find a hybrid wave.

What I would suggest based on different approaches are:
*Drop Rate & Chest Adjustment*
• Even though we are not serving them as IAP, we should definitely have much more versatile chests. 
• We probably stick to the idea of 10 cards but I don't think, it's a nice way to handle that in our case. But if we're going with that,  
    ◦ I[USERNAME_29502], we can have a chest giving only owned items. In that way, we can encourage early upgrades. 
        ▪︎ I'm opposed to giving wildcards right away, if we will have them , they should feel more unique imo. 
• Make very small collections along with the items used. 
    ◦ Making commons early at first comes from small set of items introduced. 
    ◦ In that way, we can promote more common cards early in the funnel and players can see the progression on he cards unlocked (even in the same rarity)
        ▪︎ Create a pool for the first 30 levels, use the objects in the levels with less effects. Versatile cards regardless of the rarity should be unlocked later. 
        ▪︎ Reduce the drop rate of rare / epic / legendary in both packs. 
    ◦  So what we need is that, as players unlocks new sets of items, they will have the dilemma of using already-upgraded cards or a new card which has more effects but not enough items yet. 
        ▪︎ After playing more, players can open "chapter packs" from trophy road to get more duplicates for the currently unlocked set. Towards the end of that chapter, they can upgrade their new items and the loop can be sustained for later object set in a simil[USERNAME_30025].  
*Burning / Wildcard Idea*
• Only common and uncommon cards can be burned into bones. 
    ◦ To make the UI less confusing and straightforward, burning a card should burn everything and the card itself.  
    ◦ We can let players to burn rare cards attached to level progression maybe. 
    ◦ In that way, the commons and uncommon becomes complete fodder while still keeping the value of wild card as a source of excitement. 
• Make wildcards more unique as a part of pack opening. 
• Use bones to either open a new pack or open a Wildcard pack (more costly but you can use it for upgrades directly)

<@EMPLOYEE_0012_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID> reminder that the critical damage % increase setting in Unity works like this. The value you see here are ADDED on top of the 100% damage of the item. So when base value = 100%, this means base value for critical damage for this item is 200%. So this screenshot here means the base value of this item is 0, so default is 100% (No critical damage), then by level 1 (Element 0), it adds 100, which = 200% total, so it's double damage at level 1. Then after that it's 100 + 125 = 225% critical damage at level 2. I think we might have given some items an extra 100% critical damage.

OK, so I balanced all the splash items in the game. I reduced the amount of splash items to 39 out of all the items we  have. I also removed a lot of splash from level 0 objects, so it doesn't mess with the earlier levels. <@EMPLOYEE_0005_SLACK_ID>

I also changed some of the critical % chance for lots of the items. Basically the default crit % should be around 25%. Crit items in general are not very fun when you have <10% chance. ricochet default is 35%, so I try not to shy away too much from that. The 5%-10% chance for these effects will not make the game very consistent but instead very volatile. I think we need to slow down the release of new sets. Early pace was good but then at level 60+ I felt like I can’t keep up with the intro pace of new items. Your level 60 should be level 100 , level 90 needs to be level 200 etc. imo (I’m at 29/45 items unlocked with 15-20 pack opens I’d think - I spent all my currencies on packs lol).

I have had enough early pressure to upgrade items and at some point my 3 star common item was kicking ass - I think I might have gotton lucky with epics and legendaries but they overpower common stuff quickly - needs some better tuning There. Maybe further reduce the drop rate of epics and legendaries AND/OR reduce their level 1 strength a bit further?
I think the upgrade cost of common and uncommon could be lower so they are easily accessible. Level 1 tier up cost 250 across all tiers
it could be something like 100-250-500 etc. instead of <tel:[PHONE_48749]|250-500-1000>

I think you guys tuned down how many equipped items one starts the level with. I think it’s a great idea from balancing standpoint but it got to a point where single items have no impact because if the item doesn’t exist in the level, you only get one extra set. I think we should at least do 2 sets if not 4 to make item insertion feel impactful to the gameplay. They only feel impactful if that item already exist in the level and There is no way to know before playing the level

Thank you! I also thought the collection unlock should be less frequent, the gap is growing too fast.

Unfortunately, objects are not modified for the power curve yet because it's still subject to change after the effects introducing so I sometimes changed a common to rare without changing any damage properties.

For premium packs, the epic and legendary drop rate can still be tuned down I agree.

For the item insertion, I feel similar. I don't fully grasp the new limitation but since it doesn't replace a whole set of items, it sometimes make he level harder because of the increased unique item count.
